claims.text: As-cast, homogenized HfNbTaTiZr is a single-phase BCC solid solution with no detectable intermetallic precipitates.
Aging HfNbTaTiZr at 700 °C for 24 h forms nanoscale intermetallic precipitates.
The aging-induced intermetallic precipitates are fine and coherent with the BCC matrix.
The precipitates and BCC matrix have mismatched thermal expansion.
Thermal-expansion mismatch between coherent precipitates and the matrix produces residual internal stresses.
The residual internal stresses impede dislocation glide and climb.
Precipitate-associated internal stresses govern the alloy's high-temperature strength, low-temperature hardening, and anomalous thermoelastic behavior.
The precipitate-induced internal stresses remain mechanically effective across the full range from 293 K to 1250 °C.
Aging at 700 °C for 24 h will reduce the steady-state creep rate at 1250 °C by approximately 20–30% relative to an unaged baseline.
Aging at 700 °C for 24 h will increase the elastic modulus at 1100 K by approximately 10% relative to an unaged baseline.
Aging at 700 °C for 24 h will increase microhardness after 50% cold rolling by approximately 15% relative to an unaged baseline.
The proposed mechanism applies to aging treatments between 600 and 800 °C for 12–48 h.
The proposed mechanism applies during mechanical testing from 293 K to 1250 °C at stresses no greater than 200 MPa.
